stemMd: A restaurant claims that replacing printed menus with a board will eliminate menu-printing waste. Which assumption is necessary for that specific claim?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The restaurant changes its dishes every day.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The restaurant will not continue printing menus for other uses after introducing the board.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The board costs less than one print run.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Customers will order faster from a board.

explanationMd: The conclusion is elimination, not merely reduction. Any continuing paper-menu use would leave some printing waste. The assumption rules out the residual activity that would directly contradict the absolute claim.

distractorRationale.d: Speed is not required to eliminate printing waste.
distractorRationale.e: Images do not establish whether paper menus remain.
distractorRationale.a: Change frequency may affect savings but is not required for elimination.
distractorRationale.c: Cost is separate from printing waste.
